rows.noOracleRationale: Two independent reasons, and the first is the decisive one. (1) NO CANDIDATE CAN SEE THE AXES. This vocabulary addresses the SOF marker byte, the frame's sample precision, whether a DAC arithmetic-conditioning segment is present, the per-class Huffman table count and each component's sampling factors — every one of them a field of the frame header or the entropy-coding mode. `image` 0.25 is registered by the sibling ✳️any subset and is the right reference for a JPEG raster, but its public API hands back pixels, dimensions and a colour type; it exposes no frame header, no SOFn discriminant, no DAC flag and no DHT view, and it offers no way to WRITE any of them either. `jpeg-decoder` exposes only an `ImageInfo`. A reference that cannot express the mutation cannot adjudicate it, and registering one anyway to satisfy the workflow would be selecting a weak oracle mechanically. (2) EVEN A PERFECT ORACLE WOULD BE MEASURING NOTHING AT THE BYTE LEVEL, because this repository's own `encode_jpg` writes a conforming baseline file and no other kind of JPEG at all: it emits `FF C0` for the frame marker, precision 8, a fixed three-component 4:2:0 sampling array, exactly four DHT segments and never a DAC — so every axis this vocabulary moves is normalized away on re-serialization. That is a real, documented property of the codec (stated in the vocabulary's own module docstring), not a gap. The substitutes are therefore the standard's own tables — ITU-T T.81 Table B.1 for the SOFn marker codes, §4.2 for the 8-bit precision mandate, Annex F for Huffman-only entropy coding, §B.2.4.2 for the four-table-per-class ceiling and §B.2.2 for the 1..=4 sampling factors — read against `check_baseline_conformance`, which is where the class verdict actually lives; plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property over the decoded snapshot. `mutate-jpg-jfif-1-01-baseline` measures the vocabulary there and says in as many words that it makes no byte-level claim, except in `identity-round-trip`, which does re-encode and reads both sides through the INDEPENDENT `image` reader the ✳️any subset registers.

rows.oracleRationale: Chosen over `serde_json` specifically BECAUSE it is independent: `serde_json` is already a genuine production runtime dependency of this repository (workspace-level `serde_json = "1.0.149"`), and this subset's own production code (`../🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🦀️component.rs`) declares `impl From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` / the reverse conversion — a public interop path FROM the reference's own type INTO this subset's model. A `serde_json` differential would therefore be judged by something the subject already knows how to convert from, not an independent implementation. `json` (json-rust) has no such relationship: it is a standalone recursive-descent RFC 8259 parser/serializer with its own `JsonValue`/`Object`/`Number` types unrelated to this codebase, reachable from no production file. Two real gaps versus `serde_json` (and versus this subset's own codec) are absorbed rather than hidden: `json::object::Object` stores entries in a hash-ordered binary tree keyed by an FNV-1a hash of each key (see its own source), not insertion order — RFC 8259 §4 already declares object member order insignificant, so this is covered by the SAME `ordered-json-v1` core profile (array order significant, key order never) a `serde_json` oracle would also have needed; and `json::number::Number` is a `(sign, mantissa: u64, exponent: i16)` decimal pair, not this subset's own arbitrary-precision LEXEME (RFC 8259 §6 permits arbitrary precision) — numbers are compared by parsed `f64` value, a real information-loss boundary beyond IEEE-754 double precision that the real committed fixture never crosses (verified: no number token in it exceeds 3 integer digits before any decimal point). WORKED_AROUND_DEFECT: both directions of that `Number` conversion are lossy in 0.12, and neither is a precision boundary of the format -- they move values that ARE representable as `f64`. `impl From<f64> for JsonValue` rounds INTO the decimal pair (`2.7000102824824506` dumps as `...507`, `-8.881784197001252e-16` as `...253e-16`; 2 of 9 probed values moved), and `as_f64()` rounds back OUT of it by recomputing `mantissa * 10^exponent` in floating point (the fixture's `-1.3283902924697095e-17` surface normal reads out as `...097e-17`). Both were reproduced standalone against the crate alone before being worked around, and neither is hidden: the crate's PARSER and its `dump()` are exact on every probed value, so the oracle module reaches the same `Number` through those halves -- `json::parse` of the value formatted with Rust's own shortest round-trip `{:?}` going in, `value.dump().parse::<f64>()` coming out -- and pins both the defect and the fix in its own unit tests, so a later release that fixes the conversion makes those tests fail and the workaround can go. Left unfixed, the drift is one ULP per cycle and it fails the inverse law on a defect that is not this repository's.

RFC 7493 I-JSON is a restriction of the JSON VALUE SPACE, so the reference has to be a codec that (a) reads and writes RFC 8259 text and (b) surfaces the three facts the profile turns on — the ORDERED member list of every object including duplicate names, the exact number LEXEME, and the decoded string — none of which a codec that eagerly normalizes into a hash map can report. `simplejson` does all three: `object_pairs_hook` hands back `[(name, value), ...]` in document order with duplicates intact (a `dict`-producing parser silently collapses them, which would make RFC 7493 §2.3 unobservable), `parse_int`/`parse_float` hand back the raw lexeme so §2.2's ±(2^53−1) bound is checked on the digits rather than through a lossy double, and it re-serializes, so every one of this subset's ten kinds is genuinely DIFFERENTIAL rather than merely read-back. It is deliberately not CPython's stdlib `json`: that module is registrable only as the package name `json`, which the platform's own production-purity probe would then match against every `import json` in the repository, and a probe that cannot distinguish a reference library from the language's standard library is not a probe. It is deliberately not `serde_json` either: this subset's ✳️any parent declares `impl From<serde_json::Value> for JsonValue` in production, so a `serde_json` differential would compare this implementation against something it already converts from. `simplejson` has neither relationship — no file in this repository imports it, and this subset's codec has no conversion path to or from its types.

The reference ASPRS LAS reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem. Every declared `LasMutation` kind is performed against this subset's OWN `las::raw::{Header,Vlr,Point}` types (the crate's byte-exact typed mirror of the LAS 1.0 public header block / VLR / point-data-format-0-3 records), not its friendlier `las::{Reader,Writer,Builder}` façade: the façade auto-recomputes `bounds`/`points_by_return` from whatever points are actually written and offers no way to override them, while this subset's own `LasHeader` (see its doc comment) treats bounds/points-by-return as directly retained, non-structural content — real-world LAS files frequently carry an inaccurate one, and `SetBounds`/`SetPointsByReturn` need to be able to set an arbitrary value independent of the real point distribution to be a checked mutation rather than a no-op. The raw types give exactly that control while still being the crate's own (de)serialization, so the oracle stays a genuine second producer. `SetVersion` scenarios are kept within the LAS 1.0-1.2 family (no LAS 1.3/1.4 minor value): `las::raw::Header::write_to` appends waveform/EVLR/large-file header extensions once `version.supports(..)` reports true for those newer minors, growing the header past the fixed 227 bytes this subset's own `encode_las` always emits (its own `EncodeScopeNote` states plainly: 'no LAS 1.3/1.4 extensions') — exercising 1.3/1.4 would be testing a real capability gap in the SUBJECT under the banner of a version-label mutation, not the mutation itself.

The reference ID3 implementation of the Rust ecosystem (11.5M downloads, MIT, pure Rust; its only transitive dependencies are flate2 — already linked here — plus byteorder and bitflags). It READS AND WRITES ID3v2.2/2.3/2.4, which is what makes it usable as a mutation oracle rather than only an independent reader: `Tag::read_from2` parses the tag, `Tag::write_to` re-serializes it from its own frame model alone, and `Tag::skip` independently locates the end of the ID3v2 region — the byte boundary this subset's `decode_mp3` also has to find, computed here by the reference rather than by the subject. Its ID3v1 half (`id3::v1::Tag::read_from`) is read-only, so `set-id3v1` WRITES the 128-byte trailer from the ID3v1 field layout directly (fixed-width ISO-8859-1 fields, no encoder freedom at all) and `id3::v1::Tag::read_from` reads it back independently — a genuine differential on the read side, honestly narrower on the write side. The MPEG audio frame layer is NOT this crate's business and is not claimed here: the frame walk (11-bit sync word, version/layer/bitrate/sample-rate fields, and the Layer I vs Layer II/III frame-size formula) is hand-written from ISO/IEC 11172-3 in this subset's oracle module and never calls this subset's own `find_frame_sync`/`parse_frame_header`.

Unlike several of this wave's other reference crates it genuinely both reads AND writes: `Mp4Reader::read_header`/`read_sample` parse a real `moov`/`mdat` into typed tracks and samples, and `Mp4Writer::write_start`/`add_track`/`write_sample`/`write_end` re-mux a fresh, real, spec-valid file from them (confirmed against the real derived fixture before this manifest was written — a round trip through `mp4` alone reproduces every sample's payload bytes exactly). Every declared mutation kind is therefore performed for real through `mp4`'s own writer, not synthesized, and scenarios are typed `@mode-differential` per the fleet brief. `mp4`'s public surface only covers a single AVC (h264) `avc1` sample entry per track with a single SPS/single PPS and a hardcoded 4-byte NAL length size — the exact shape of the real fixture's own H.264 stream, so this is not a narrowing the oracle imposes, it is the format the real input already is.

The reference Wavefront OBJ reader of the Rust ecosystem. OBJ has no reference WRITER — it is a plain-text grammar — so the oracle writes the grammar directly and tobj serves as the independent reader that makes the comparison meaningful. Whitespace, numeric formatting and statement order are writer freedom; the vertex set, face topology and counts are normative.

OBJ has no reference WRITER in the Rust ecosystem — it is a plain-text grammar — so this subset's oracle applies every declared mutation kind by direct grammar manipulation (mirroring the same precedent the shared `tobj` mesh-creation oracle already uses) and `tobj` serves as the independent reader every oracle and subject result is projected through before comparison. `tobj` alone is not enough to judge this vocabulary: it triangulates, re-indexes per `o`/`g` model and drops every row no face references, so 14 of the 22 declared kinds move nothing in its reading at all. The projection therefore composes that `tobj` mesh reading with this module's own `oracle_document_projection` -- declared `v`/`vt`/`vn` row counts and per-component extent, the `mtllib` reference, the `g`/`o` membership spans, the `usemtl`/`s` run starts and the retained comment lines -- and the case asserts in role that every kind but `no-mutation` actually moves it. That document half is read by this module's independent grammar parser, which never touches the subject's `decode_obj`, so it stays a second reader rather than a self-comparison.

Typed, step-by-step PDF writer with explicit control over catalog, page tree, media boxes and content streams — the creation reference. Deterministic given the same call sequence, no network, no system dependencies, runs on Windows/macOS/Linux.

PDF document-manipulation library exposing object-level editing, page insert/delete, content-stream rewriting and an independent parser — serves both as the editing oracle and as the independent reader that proves a subject's output is parseable.

Text extraction is the one PDF capability this repository has no Rust reference for. `lopdf` — the registered editing and parsing oracle — exposes the object graph and the raw content streams, but reconstructing a page's reading order means decoding the font's /Encoding and /ToUnicode CMaps, undoing ligature and glyph-index mappings and re-assembling text-showing operators into lines; it does none of that, and no other crate linked by the oracle host does either. `pypdf` implements exactly that layer and is the reference every Python PDF toolchain builds text extraction on. Scoped to the text layer only: page geometry, object structure and rendering stay with the existing oracles.

rows.noOracleRationale: `s.stdio.semio` is the ENVELOPE union over all eighteen semio subsets; there is no third-party crate that reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, and there could not be one authoritative over a vocabulary whose eighteen wrapper variants each embed another semio-native subset's own mutation enum. What this subset OWNS is not the payload semantics — those belong to the eighteen arms and are covered by their own leaf fixtures and their own cases — but the envelope-level ROUTING: does a wrapped mutation whose arm matches the base snapshot's arm thread through, does a MISMATCHED one get refused with `mutation.target-missing` instead of silently corrupting the document, and is `set-snapshot` genuinely the only verb that can change the subset kind. Every scenario is written against exactly that, with a projection the envelope can answer without naming any arm's snapshot type: `{schema, subset, diagnostics, matchesReference}`. Confidence comes from the committed `(before, mutation, after, diff)` specification vector under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/📄set-snapshot/🧪️tests/`, already unit-tested inside the production crate, plus the routing and inverse laws as metamorphic properties. Honest limits, recorded rather than papered over: the eighteen delegating arms are exercised against each arm's OWN empty snapshot rather than a real-world document, because no real-world `.semio` artifact exists outside this repository and the committed example assets can only be decoded through `store::ArtifactDsl`/`store::ArtifactPack`, traits reached solely via a private extern-crate alias that nothing re-exports — the same structural gap wave 7 recorded for `kit`, `object`, `text` and `table`. Re-exporting those two traits would let this case read the committed `.dsl.semio` examples directly and is the single change that would most strengthen it. WAVE-14 RE-SURVEY (cross-language differential oracles, ticket 26/08/23): a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language was built for five sibling subsets in this same artifact and works end to end, so the route was re-examined here and REJECTED on two concrete, nameable blockers rather than on absence. First, the envelope's own committed documents declare the wrapped arm OPAQUE: the snapshot grammar's `document = artifact-mark subset-line REST` hands off to the arm's own grammar, the binary protocol models the wrapped pack as one opaque trailing `payload` chain, and the mutations grammar is `op = "noMutation" | tag ":" REST`. An envelope-level second implementation can therefore reproduce both committed carriers byte for byte - and it can - but it can say nothing about whether a DELEGATED verb changed the arm it reached, which is exactly what eighteen of this vocabulary's twenty kinds measure. Answering that honestly needs a second implementation of eighteen separate subset vocabularies, not of this one. Second, nothing lets the two languages read the same arm input: this subset exports `parse_semio_envelope_dsl`/`print_semio_envelope_dsl` and `decode_semio_envelope_pack`/`encode_semio_envelope_pack` but NO JSON bridge for `SemioSnapshot` or `SemioMutation`, so the arm snapshots and the wrapped verbs can only be constructed in Rust, inside the subject crate, where a second language cannot see them. Registering a Python oracle that merely restated the routing table would be a transcribed expectation wearing an oracle's name - our own answer on both sides - and is the one thing this platform exists to prevent, so it was not done. The two changes that would unblock a real differential here, in order of leverage: export a JSON bridge for `SemioSnapshot`/`SemioMutation` the way `✳️cad` and `✳️document` already do, and re-export `store::ArtifactDsl`/`store::ArtifactPack` so an external adapter can decode the committed example assets. A third, smaller finding recorded here rather than filed away: the committed snapshot grammar's `subset-tag` production still lists only thirteen tags (brep, mesh, model, value, document, cad, drawing, image, video, audio, animation, presentation, flow) while this catalog and the sibling mutations grammar both declare eighteen arms - `text`, `table`, `graph`, `object` and `kit` are missing from it.

rows.noOracleRationale: Two independent reasons. (1) THE QUESTION IS NOT ONE A PACKAGE ANSWERS. This vocabulary asks whether a decoded document is inside Adobe TIFF 6.0 Part 1's Baseline class, read on five specific fields of IFD 0 — `Compression` (259) restricted to {1, 2, 32773}, `PhotometricInterpretation` (262) to 0..=3, `BitsPerSample` (258) to {1, 4, 8}, `TileWidth`/`TileLength` (322/323) absent because Baseline is strip-organized, and `StripOffsets` (273) present when it is not tiled. `image` 0.25's TIFF surface is a single-IFD raster codec: it decodes pixels and re-encodes them under its own choice of those very tags, and exposes no API to set an arbitrary compression, an out-of-range photometric or a tile-organized IFD. It could not perform any row of this vocabulary, and it holds no opinion about class membership to be compared against. (2) FOUR OF SIX KINDS ARE NOT BYTE-OBSERVABLE THROUGH THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN ENCODER EITHER: `encode_tiff` regenerates every one of `CORE_STRIP_TAGS` from the raster it is about to write, so `set-compression`, `set-photometric-interpretation`, `set-bits-per-sample` and `set-strip-offsets` are normalized away on re-serialization — a documented property of the codec, stated in the vocabulary's own module docstring, and the same constraint PNG's IHDR is under. Only the two tile kinds survive, because `TileWidth`/`TileLength` sit outside `CORE_STRIP_TAGS` and are carried verbatim. The substitutes are therefore TIFF 6.0's own tag-value tables read against `check_tiff_baseline_conformance`, which is where the class verdict lives, plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property over the decoded snapshot. `mutate-tiff-6-0-baseline` measures the vocabulary there and says in as many words that it makes no byte-level claim for those four kinds; its `identity-round-trip` does re-encode, and reads both sides through the independent IFD reader the ✳️any subset registers.
